uncertainties: The Lesson 1 chart (pp. 22-23) does not print a distinct single-symbol transliteration column for consonants (e.g. ʾ, ḥ, ṣ, š) — only the italicized English name-spellings (e.g. 'alef, chet, tsade, sin, shin), which are captured in nameEnglish; a footnote on p. 22 says the accent mark on these names 'indicates which syllable is stressed when pronouncing the name of the letter,' confirming they are pronunciation guides for the name, not a transliteration scheme for the consonant sound. translit is therefore null for all 23 letters.

Appendix A 'Phonology' pp. a-3 to a-6 (PDF 143-146) covers only the Masoretic/ancient/Israeli vowel systems, vowel length classes, syllable typing, word stress, and matres lectionis (א/ה/ו/י as vowel markers) — it contains no consonant alphabet chart, so it supplied no cross-check data (confirming or contradicting) for this letter inventory.

The printed chart on pp. 22-23 includes 'Script (Final)' and 'Print (Final)' columns showing cursive-style and block-style letterform variants for every consonant and each final form; presence noted per instructions but glyph variants were not transcribed.

P. 22 highlights 'Four consonants pronounced in the back of the throat are often called gutturals' followed by a highlighted glyph group; read as א ה ח ע (alef, he, chet, ayin), matching the four rows in the chart whose Pronunciation is a back-of-throat/silent description ('glottal stop or silent', 'h in Hat', 'ch in BaCH', 'pharyngeal or silent'). Scan clarity around the highlight box left some doubt about exact glyph order, though the letter identities are unambiguous from the pronunciation column.

P. 21 also prints a secondary table of consonant pairs that sound alike (e.g. א/ע silent, ב/ו like v, ח/כ like ch, ט/ת like t, כ/ק like k, ס/שׂ like s) with an adjoining column of name-abbreviations (e.g. 'alef/oyin') that appeared handwritten/cursive in the scan rather than typeset; excluded from this transcription per the instruction to ignore handwritten annotations.
